# hush_cloudflare_r2_access_privilege (Data Source)

Use this data source to retrieve information about a Cloudflare R2 access privilege in the Hush Security platform.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "hush_cloudflare_r2_access_privilege" "example" {
  id = "apr-eu12345678"
}

output "permission" {
  value = data.hush_cloudflare_r2_access_privilege.example.permission
}

output "buckets" {
  value = data.hush_cloudflare_r2_access_privilege.example.buckets
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) The unique identifier of the Cloudflare R2 access privilege

### Read-Only

- `all_buckets` (Boolean) Grant an object permission every bucket of the account, including buckets created later. An object permission needs `buckets` or `all_buckets = true`, so the widest grant never comes from leaving `buckets` out. Not valid with an admin permission
- `buckets` (Set of String) The buckets an object permission reaches: 1 to 1000 R2 bucket names. Names are not checked against the account, so a misspelled one, or one in another jurisdiction, gives credentials that S3 refuses for it. Not valid with an admin permission
- `description` (String) The description of the Cloudflare R2 access privilege
- `jurisdiction` (String) The jurisdiction of the buckets: `default`, `eu`, `fedramp` or `us`. A bucket in a jurisdiction answers only on that jurisdiction's S3 endpoint, so one privilege covers one jurisdiction. Defaults to `default`
- `name` (String) The name of the Cloudflare R2 access privilege
- `permission` (String) The access level of the R2 tokens, as the Cloudflare dashboard names it: `object_read_write` or `object_read_only` reach the objects of `buckets`, or of every bucket with `all_buckets`; `admin_read_write` or `admin_read_only` are account wide, and `admin_read_write` can also manage buckets
- `type` (String) The type of access privilege
